source.title: Generalization Comparison of Deep Neural Networks via Output Sensitivity
source.authors: Mahsa Forouzesh; Farnood Salehi; Patrick Thiran

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares test loss and output sensitivity across architectures and regularization settings. These experiments bear conceptually on generalization, but do not reproduce the original claim versions’ specific methods or measures.
record.gate_note: The paper reports experiments comparing architecture and regularization choices, along with sensitivity and test loss. It does not test random-label memorization, optimizer comparisons, batch-size effects, or removal of memorized examples. Sensitivity is input-output perturbation, not the magnitude-aware weight perturbation measure in V7.
record.test_reason: The study measures cross-entropy test loss and sensitivity to input perturbations. It does not establish the classification-error effects named in V2, V3 or V6. This distinction matters here: Section 6.2 explicitly separates loss from accuracy, and Appendix Table 2 reports a negative correlation between loss and classification error before calibration. Depth-versus-width comparisons also do not isolate widening past interpolation. Input sensitivity does not measure V7's magnitude-aware weight sharpness.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors propose input sensitivity as a strong indicator of overfitting and a loose predictor of test loss without labeled evaluation data, particularly among networks with near-zero training loss. They explicitly qualify the approximation, distinguish loss from classification accuracy, and do not establish causality.
record.recipe_differences: Measures input-output sensitivity and test loss across architecture and training choices; it does not reproduce random-label memorization, the weight perturbation measure, or the optimizer and batch-size comparisons in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The relation between sensitivity and test loss varies with the measurement location: sensitivity before the softmax has a stronger reported correlation than sensitivity after it. The authors also report that the sensitivity-loss approximation fits less well with fewer training samples and early in training.

fits_no_version.finding: CNNs have lower cross-entropy test loss than FCs in the reported CIFAR-10 comparisons; narrower, deeper networks can also have lower loss than wider, shallower networks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architecture choices affect cross-entropy test loss in the studied classifiers.

fits_no_version.finding: Dropout, batch normalization and max-pooling reduce test loss and input sensitivity in the reported settings. Appendix Figure 6 extends the CIFAR-10 dropout comparison across additional FC and CNN configurations; Figures 8 and 9 report MNIST and CIFAR-100 comparisons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: These training and architecture choices can reduce cross-entropy loss alongside input sensitivity.

fits_no_version.finding: Input sensitivity correlates with test loss across configurations. Figure 1 reports a correlation of 0.9707 between their logarithms; the association depends on measurement location, initialization, training stage and sample size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sensitivity to input perturbations can serve as a conditional proxy for cross-entropy test loss.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix Table 2 reports loss–classification-error correlations of -0.797 before temperature calibration and 0.137 afterward for the studied MNIST networks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-entropy loss need not rank classification error reliably in these experiments.

record.problems: Experiments use subsets of the training data (1000 samples for CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, 6000 for MNIST); several comparisons are conveyed through plots without exact test-loss values in the text. The sensitivity-to-loss relation relies on stated approximations and assumptions, and the authors explicitly distinguish correlation from causality.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-version rows were identified. Other plot series compare initialization choices or sensitivity against alternative metrics, but do not directly test a listed version.

untested.parts: No experiment compares fitting and held-out accuracy for natural versus fixed random labels.
No classification-error sweep past an identified zero-training-error width threshold for a fixed architecture.
CNN-versus-FC classification error, the contribution of local connectivity, learned sparse connections, and convolutionally initialized FC networks are not established.
Dropout's effect on classification error, small-data failure regimes, excessive-dropout underfitting, and joint removal with weight decay under augmentation are not established.
No magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness measurement or comparison against norm- and margin-based gap rankings.
No memorized-example removal and retraining experiment.

record.verdict_notes: The reported loss reductions are valid study findings. Their cannot_determine states concern the listed claim versions, not whether those loss reductions occurred. The study is not an original source for any listed version.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or comparison of natural-label and random-label test performance.

The paper compares depth and width for multilayer FC and CNNs; it does not test one-hidden-layer networks specifically, or identify the width required to reach zero training error and sweep past that threshold.
No learned sparse local connections, convolutional initialization of a fully connected network, CIFAR-100, or SVHN comparison is reported in the main experiments.
No adaptive-versus-SGD optimizer comparison or broader optimizer tuning.
No batch-size comparison or fixed-epoch large-batch training experiment.

Dropout is compared in some FC and CNN settings. The paper does not test very small training sets as a failure regime, excessive dropout underfitting, or jointly removing dropout and weight decay with data augmentation.

The paper measures sensitivity to input perturbations and its relation to test loss; it does not measure magnitude-aware weight perturbations or compare their ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
No memorized-example identification, removal, or retraining comparison.

rows.subject: Fully-connected neural networks (FC), 4–7 layers
rows.size_stated: hidden units varied from 100 to 500; same width in hidden layers
rows.operation_detail: Compared test loss across FC networks with different depths and widths.
rows.measure: Test loss L; qualitative comparison of depth and width
rows.value: The paper reports that narrower 5-layer networks (100, 120, and 140 units) perform better than a wide 4-layer network (500 units); the matched pair has the same Safter and L.
rows.uncertainty: Coordinates averaged over 10 runs; no error bar stated for this comparison.
rows.note: The reported measure is test loss, not test error. This depth-width comparison does not isolate widening beyond an established zero-training-error threshold.
rows.check: Comparing different depths and widths using test loss does not establish how classification error changes when a fixed architecture is widened beyond its interpolation threshold. The equal-loss pair is the 4-layer, 500-unit network and the 5-layer, 165-unit network; the 100-, 120- and 140-unit networks have lower loss.

rows.subject: Convolutional neural networks (CNN), 1–4 layers
rows.operation_detail: Compared test loss across CNNs of different depths and widths.
rows.measure: Test loss L; qualitative comparison of depth and width
rows.value: The authors report a similar trend for CNNs: a narrower, deeper CNN is preferable to a wider, shallower CNN.
rows.uncertainty: Coordinates averaged over 10 runs; no error bar stated for this comparison.
rows.note: The comparison does not establish behavior specifically beyond the width needed for zero training error.
rows.check: Depth and width change together, no interpolation threshold is identified, and the outcome is test loss rather than classification error.

rows.subject: Fully-connected neural networks (FC) and convolutional neural networks (CNN)
rows.size_stated: Comparison includes a 3-layer FC with 140 units per layer and a 1-layer CNN with 5 channels and 100 units; both have 450k parameters
rows.operation_detail: Compared test loss for FC and CNN architectures, including a matched-parameter pair.
rows.baseline: 3-layer FC with 140 units per layer; 450k parameters
rows.value: The 1-layer CNN with 5 channels and 100 units; 450k parameters; the authors state it has remarkably lower sensitivity and test loss than the FC.
rows.uncertainty: Coordinates averaged over 10 runs; no error bar stated for the pair.
rows.note: The paper also states that CNNs with the same parameter count have lower sensitivity and test loss than FCs, and that some CNNs with more parameters do as well.
rows.check: The matched-parameter CNN has lower cross-entropy loss and input sensitivity. Neither measurement establishes lower classification error, which the paper explicitly distinguishes from loss.

rows.subject: Fully-connected neural networks (FC) and convolutional neural networks (CNN)
rows.size_stated: CNNs: 450k to 10M parameters; 3-layer FCs: 320k to 1.7M parameters
rows.operation_detail: Compared adding a convolutional layer with adding a fully connected layer to a one-hidden-layer FC baseline.
rows.baseline: One-hidden-layer FC baseline; comparison adds either an FC layer or a convolutional layer.
rows.value: The authors report that adding a convolutional layer gives lower test loss than adding a fully connected layer; CNNs also have lower sensitivity and test loss in the reported comparisons.
rows.uncertainty: Coordinates averaged over 10 runs; no error bar stated for this comparison.
rows.note: The paper does not test learned sparse local connections or FC networks initialized from trained CNNs.
rows.check: The layer-addition comparison establishes lower test loss, not the lower classification error named in V3. It also does not isolate local connectivity from weight sharing.

rows.subject: Fully-connected neural networks (FC) with and without dropout
rows.size_stated: 4-layer FC; hidden-layer width varied from 100 to 500
rows.operation_detail: Compared FC networks trained with and without dropout.
rows.value: The paper reports a shift toward lower test loss when dropout is applied.
rows.uncertainty: Coordinates averaged over 10 runs; no error bar stated.
rows.note: The paper does not report the dropout rate for this comparison in the cited discussion.
rows.check: Dropout lowers cross-entropy test loss in the reported comparison, but classification-error improvement is not established.

rows.subject: Convolutional neural networks (CNN) with and without dropout
rows.operation_detail: Compared CNNs trained with and without dropout.
rows.value: The paper reports a shift toward lower test loss when dropout is applied.
rows.uncertainty: Coordinates averaged over 10 runs; no error bar stated.
rows.note: The paper does not report the dropout rate for this comparison in the cited discussion.
rows.check: Dropout lowers cross-entropy test loss in the reported comparison, but classification-error improvement is not established.

rows.subject: Fully-connected neural networks (FC) and convolutional neural networks (CNN) with batch normalization
rows.size_stated: FC and CNN configurations; multiple depths and widths
rows.operation_detail: Compared networks trained with and without batch normalization.
rows.value: The authors report a shift toward lower test loss with batch normalization, particularly a dramatic decrease for the FC comparison.
rows.uncertainty: Coordinates averaged over 10 runs; no error bar stated.
rows.note: Batch normalization is outside the listed claim versions.
rows.check: The reported batch-normalization effect on loss is outside the listed versions.

rows.subject: Convolutional neural networks (CNN) with max-pooling
rows.operation_detail: Compared CNNs trained with and without max-pooling.
rows.value: The authors report a shift toward lower test loss when max-pooling is applied.
rows.uncertainty: Coordinates averaged over 10 runs; no error bar stated.
rows.note: Max-pooling is outside the listed claim versions.
rows.check: The reported max-pooling effect on loss is outside the listed versions.

rows.subject: Fully-connected neural networks (FC) and convolutional neural networks (CNN) with dropout and batch normalization
rows.operation_detail: Measured output sensitivity after training for networks with and without regularization.
rows.baseline: Networks without the respective regularization method
rows.value: The paper reports that dropout, batch normalization, and max-pooling shift points toward lower sensitivity alongside lower test loss.
rows.uncertainty: Coordinates averaged over 10 runs; no error bar stated.
rows.locator: Section 5.2, Figures 2(d) and 2(e); Appendix F, Figure 6
rows.note: These are input perturbation measurements and do not test V7's magnitude-aware weight sharpness.
rows.check: Input-perturbation sensitivity is not magnitude-aware weight sharpness. Correct the locator: Figure 6 is in Appendix E. Include max-pooling in the subject if retaining it in the reported value.
